svg.title: Prime addressing: an address is a product of primes
svg.desc: The integers 1 to 60 on a grid with primes highlighted. The composite address 30 is joined by curves to its prime coordinates 2, 3 and 5, and all multiples of 5, the records sharing that factor, are ringed. A table of exponent vectors shows that a gcd is the component-wise minimum of exponents.
svg.text: Prime addressing: an address is a product of primes
records 1 … 60 (blue = prime; ring = multiple of 5, shares a factor with 30)
n is in the answer iff 5 | n.
An address is a product of primes; a read admits records that share a factor (gcd > 1) or the longest matching prime n-let,
Prime exponents are the coordinates: gcd is the component-wise minimum, so shared factors are read off exactly.
